term:coupling.oneliner: Greenhouse gases have already rewired the invisible threads linking weather across the planet.
term:coupling.why: Shows that atmospheric links between distant regions are changing because of human forcing, so these pathways are not fixed.

term:coupling.title: Coupled Ocean-Atmosphere Dynamics in a Machine Learning Earth System Model
term:coupling.our_title: Ocean and Atmosphere Learn to Speak the Same Language
term:coupling.oneliner: The neural network model Ola reproduces El Niño for the first time by modeling the ocean and atmosphere as a single system.
term:coupling.why: A machine learning Earth system model reproduces coupled El Nino dynamics, showing the ocean and atmosphere evolve together.

term:coupling.title: SamudrACE: Fast and Accurate Coupled Climate Modeling with 3D Ocean and Atmosphere Emulators
term:coupling.our_title: SamudrACE: A Climate Orchestra Without a Conductor
term:coupling.oneliner: A neural network emulator combines atmosphere and ocean into a single climate ensemble that plays 1500 years in one day.
term:coupling.why: Shows realistic ENSO variability emerges only when ocean and atmosphere are coupled in a climate model emulator.

term:cpc.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:cpc.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:cpc.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:cpc.why: Explains how climate normals for Nino 3.4 sea surface temperatures are estimated and notes limits of the standard method CPC uses.

term:cusum.title: Detecting Regime Transitions in Dynamical Systems via the Mixup Euler Characteristic Profile
term:cusum.our_title: Fingerprints of Chaos: How Trajectory Geometry Reveals the Moment of a Regime Shift
term:cusum.oneliner: By comparing the shape of trajectory intersections before and after a transition, a new method pinpoints when a system changes behavior, even in noisy signals.
term:cusum.why: Compares CUSUM to a topological method for regime shifts, finding CUSUM less accurate when the change is gradual or noisy.

term:dynstat.title: Hierarchical Testing of a Hybrid Machine Learning-Physics Global Atmosphere Model
term:dynstat.our_title: A Student Who Learned Physics from a Textbook
term:dynstat.oneliner: The hybrid atmospheric model NeuralGCM passes an exam on cyclones, El Niño, and anomalous warming, but stumbles in the stratosphere.
term:dynstat.why: Finds biases remain under plus 3K and plus 4K warming, showing machine learning struggles outside its training distribution.

term:dynstat.title: Diffusion Models Bridge Deep Learning and Physics in ENSO Forecasting
term:dynstat.our_title: Neural Network Denoises the Ocean and Predicts El Niño Two Years Ahead
term:dynstat.oneliner: A diffusion model trained only on ocean temperature delivers probabilistic El Niño forecasts up to 26 months ahead and internally reproduces the classic physics of the oscillation.
term:dynstat.why: Shows a diffusion model reproduces historical extreme El Nino events, adding nuance to statistical model limits in strong events.

term:dynstat.title: Coupled Ocean-Atmosphere Dynamics in a Machine Learning Earth System Model
term:dynstat.our_title: Ocean and Atmosphere Learn to Speak the Same Language
term:dynstat.oneliner: The neural network model Ola reproduces El Niño for the first time by modeling the ocean and atmosphere as a single system.
term:dynstat.why: Shows a neural network Earth system model forecasts El Nino with skill close to a physics model, an example of neural networks in climate.

term:eei.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
term:eei.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
term:eei.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
term:eei.why: Record low planetary albedo meant Earth absorbed more sunlight, adding to the energy imbalance and 2023 warming.

term:eei.title: Recent Weakening of the Global Radiative Feedback
term:eei.our_title: The Climate Has Become Worse at Shedding Heat
term:eei.oneliner: Over the past thirty years, Earth has become less efficient at radiating excess heat into space.
term:eei.why: Radiative feedback weakened, so Earth sheds heat less efficiently for each degree of warming, making a larger imbalance more likely.

term:elnino.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:elnino.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:elnino.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:elnino.why: Supports the 2-7 year cycle and links ENSO to global droughts and monsoons.

term:elnino.title: Resolving the Paradox of Changing El Ni\~no-Monsoon Relation through Synchronization of Chaotic Oscillators
term:elnino.our_title: The Dance of Two Pendulums: Why the Monsoon Can Be Predicted 18 Months Ahead
term:elnino.oneliner: The Indian monsoon and deep tropical ocean waters resonate with an 18-month delay, and this connection does not weaken over time.
term:elnino.why: Shows a stable link between El Niño and Indian monsoon rainfall, supporting the weak monsoon impact.

term:elnino.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:elnino.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:elnino.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:elnino.why: Refines how the central Pacific warming that defines El Niño is measured.

term:era5.title: Partial recovery of meter-scale surface weather
term:era5.oneliner: Meteorologists can now see weather down to ten meters.
term:era5.why: It shows ERA5 near surface temperature misses local meter scale variability over land, reducing error by 6 percent.

term:ersst.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:ersst.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:ersst.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:ersst.why: It questions the 30 year climate normals used for SST anomalies like the ONI and proposes a real time filter.

term:ersst.title: Probabilistic reconstruction of global sea surface temperature using generative diffusion models
term:ersst.our_title: The Ocean as a Draft: Diffusion Model Reveals All Possible Temperatures
term:ersst.oneliner: The SAGE neural network turns sparse measurements into a full fan of plausible ocean temperature maps, honestly showing where confidence is high and where it is nearly zero.
term:ersst.why: It shows deterministic SST reconstructions may miss uncertainty, which is a caveat for comparing 1877 with today.

term:lanina.title: Spatio-temporal Patterns between ENSO and Weather-related Power Outages in the Continental United States
term:lanina.our_title: The Ocean Conducts Blackouts: How La Niña Steers the US Power Grid
term:lanina.oneliner: La Niña raises the number of weather-related power outages in the US, and by century's end, heat could increase them 26-fold.
term:lanina.why: Shows La Nina phases increase weather related power outages in the US by altering extreme rainfall and heatwaves.

term:lanina.title: CNN-based forecasting of early winter NAO using sea surface temperature
term:lanina.our_title: The Ocean Whispers Early: Neural Network Hears the Atlantic Winter Three Months Ahead
term:lanina.oneliner: A convolutional neural network reads sea surface temperatures and predicts the European winter more accurately than linear models.
term:lanina.why: Finds La Nina shifts the North Atlantic Oscillation in early winter, part of its mirrored weather effects.

term:lanina.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:lanina.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:lanina.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:lanina.why: Provides a method to estimate climate normals and anomalies used to identify the cold Nino 3.4 patches that define La Nina.

term:lead.title: Distillation of CNN Ensemble Results for Enhanced Long-Term Prediction of the ENSO Phenomenon
term:lead.our_title: Selecting the Best El Niño Predictors from a Model Ensemble
term:lead.oneliner: Among 40 climate model forecasts, some members predict El Niño two years ahead noticeably better than the ensemble average.
term:lead.why: Compares ENSO forecast skill at 1-month and 23-month leads, showing accuracy depends strongly on lead time.

term:lead.title: Long-term prediction of ENSO with physics-guided Deep Echo State Networks
term:lead.our_title: El Niño Can Be Predicted a Year and a Half in Advance
term:lead.oneliner: Warm and cold phases of the Pacific Ocean are now visible long before they hit the weather.
term:lead.why: Finds ENSO predictability declines with lead, with a roughly 30-month horizon from error-growth analysis.

term:lead.title: Entropic learning enables skilful forecasts of ENSO phase at up to two years lead time
term:lead.our_title: Council of Sages: How Entropy Predicts El Niño Two Years Ahead
term:lead.oneliner: An ensemble of entropy-based models, trained solely on satellite data, forecasts the El Niño phase up to 24 months ahead with skill comparable to the best dynamical systems.
term:lead.why: Shows probabilistic ENSO phase forecasts can retain skill at 22-24 month leads, adding nuance to longer-lead expectations.

term:lead.title: Why is Seasonal Climate Predictable Beyond the Limit of Deterministic Predictability set by Chaos?
term:lead.our_title: Seasonal Climate Is Predictable Beyond Chaos
term:lead.oneliner: Monsoon and El Niño behave like two pendulums lagging each other by half a period: by tracking one, you can predict the other 18 months ahead, even though chaos promised only six months.
term:lead.why: Explains long lead monsoon predictability via lag synchronization with El Nino, a caveat to the idea that lead 6 errors are always normal.

term:lead.title: Prediction Beyond the Medium Range with an Atmosphere-Ocean Model that Combines Physics-based Modeling and Machine Learning
term:lead.our_title: A Translator That Learned the Language of the Ocean
term:lead.oneliner: A hybrid model, pairing physics with machine learning, predicts El Niño months ahead and skips the supercomputers.
term:lead.why: Measures skill of a hybrid atmosphere ocean model at 3 to 7 month leads for El Nino and tropical rainfall patterns.

term:mjo.title: A Simple Intermediate Coupled MJO-ENSO Model: Multiscale Interactions and ENSO Complexity
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Typhoon and Current: How El Niño Is Born
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model connects fast wind bursts, multi-year ocean rhythms, and decadal shifts, reproducing the full diversity of El Niño.
term:mjo.why: A coupled model shows MJO wind forcing can trigger different El Niño types, matching the timing role described on the dashboard.

term:mjo.title: A Stochastic Conceptual Model for the Coupled ENSO and MJO
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Ocean and Atmosphere Rhythms
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model links the two major tropical oscillations and reproduces their statistics.
term:mjo.why: Stochastic model links MJO wind bursts to ENSO variability, showing how random wind activity can shape El Nino timing.

term:nino3.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:nino3.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:nino3.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:nino3.why: Caveats on estimating equatorial Pacific sea surface temperature anomalies; record comparisons depend on baseline choices.

term:nino34.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:nino34.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:nino34.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:nino34.why: Shows a method to estimate sea surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region more reliably as the climate warms.

term:nino34.title: Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026
term:nino34.our_title: El Niño 2026: Two Barometers, One Forecast
term:nino34.oneliner: Two independent methods gave conflicting forecasts for 2026, so the authors combined them into a probabilistic outlook.
term:nino34.why: Forecasts the 2026 El Niño magnitude at 0.84 degrees Celsius using the Niño 3.4 anomaly measure.

term:nino4.title: Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026
term:nino4.our_title: El Niño 2026: Two Barometers, One Forecast
term:nino4.oneliner: Two independent methods gave conflicting forecasts for 2026, so the authors combined them into a probabilistic outlook.
term:nino4.why: Forecasts the type of El Nino (Eastern or Central Pacific), supporting the eastern/central event distinction in the statement.

term:ohc.title: A Summer Meridional Subsurface Temperature Dipole Mode in the South China Sea
term:ohc.our_title: Ocean Seesaw: The Hidden Heat Exchange in the South China Sea
term:ohc.oneliner: Beneath the surface of the South China Sea, north and south swap heat like two ends of a seesaw, and the monsoon and El Niño are pulling the strings.
term:ohc.why: Explains how monsoon wind stress curl moves upper ocean heat between northern and southern South China Sea.

term:ohc.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:ohc.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:ohc.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:ohc.why: Shows that upper ocean warming and stratification change ENSO strength, supporting the idea that a warmer ocean is a different system.

term:oni.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:oni.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:oni.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:oni.why: Proposes a method for estimating the baseline average used for Niño 3.4 anomalies, noting standard 30-year averages may not suit a warming climate.

term:percentile.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:percentile.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:percentile.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:percentile.why: It describes estimating climate normals and anomalies against seasonally varying baselines, so deviations are relative to the time of year.

term:pmel.title: Realistic ENSO Dynamics Requires a Damped Nonlinear Recharge Oscillator
term:pmel.our_title: A Pendulum Rocked by Gusts of Wind
term:pmel.oneliner: To understand the whims of El Niño and La Niña, scientists built a model of a pendulum with friction and random kicks.
term:pmel.why: The recharge oscillator framework links ENSO cycles to subsurface heat content, the warm water volume these buoys track.

term:pmel.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:pmel.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:pmel.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:pmel.why: Finds that subsurface warming connects to surface warming with a lag, supporting the idea that El Nino is charged below the surface.

term:roni.title: Resolving the Paradox of Changing El Ni\~no-Monsoon Relation through Synchronization of Chaotic Oscillators
term:roni.our_title: The Dance of Two Pendulums: Why the Monsoon Can Be Predicted 18 Months Ahead
term:roni.oneliner: The Indian monsoon and deep tropical ocean waters resonate with an 18-month delay, and this connection does not weaken over time.
term:roni.why: Shows Pacific only ENSO indices miss the global tropical signal, supporting a relative index like RONI.

term:shout.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:shout.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:shout.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:shout.why: Shows how the ONI anomaly baseline is estimated and that standard 30 year normals can be biased in a changing climate.

term:shout.title: Changepoint Detection As Model Selection: A General Framework
term:shout.our_title: Breaking Points: How a Restorer Cleans Data
term:shout.oneliner: The IRFL method turns changepoint detection into a model selection problem, iteratively filtering out false signals.
term:shout.why: Formal changepoint detection can flag turning points, including ENSO events, but it is model based, not rule based.

term:soi.title: Statistics of stochastic entropy for recorded transitions between ENSO states
term:soi.oneliner: Transitions between El Niño and La Niña turn out to be statistically ordinary events, not extreme entropy spikes.
term:soi.why: Uses daily Southern Oscillation Index data to track transitions between El Nino and La Nina phases.

term:t300.title: Prediction Beyond the Medium Range with an Atmosphere-Ocean Model that Combines Physics-based Modeling and Machine Learning
term:t300.our_title: A Translator That Learned the Language of the Ocean
term:t300.oneliner: A hybrid model, pairing physics with machine learning, predicts El Niño months ahead and skips the supercomputers.
term:t300.why: A hybrid model uses heat content of the top 300 m ocean to predict El Niño, showing this layer stores heat relevant to ENSO.

term:tao.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:tao.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:tao.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:tao.why: It questions standard 30 year normals and tests a real time filter on equatorial Pacific winds and sea surface temperatures.

term:teleconnection.title: Climate change alters teleconnections
term:teleconnection.oneliner: Greenhouse gases have already rewired the invisible threads linking weather across the planet.
term:teleconnection.why: Shows observed teleconnection patterns shifted and links this to human forcing, so the links are not fixed.

term:teleconnection.title: Metastability, atmospheric midlatitude circulation regimes and large-scale teleconnection: a data-driven approach
term:teleconnection.our_title: Rooms of the Winter Sky: How the Atmosphere Chooses the Weather
term:teleconnection.oneliner: In winter, the Northern Hemisphere's atmosphere can spend weeks in one of four 'rooms'—stable circulation regimes—and the transitions between them follow hidden rules.
term:teleconnection.why: Explains how recurrent midlatitude circulation regimes relate to large-scale teleconnections, the atmospheric circulation pathway.

term:teleconnection.title: Unraveling the mystery of tropical monsoon long-term prediction
term:teleconnection.our_title: Network catches the monsoon beyond the horizon
term:teleconnection.oneliner: A global web of temperature links predicts rains in four tropical regions 4–10 months ahead more accurately than seasonal models.
term:teleconnection.why: Demonstrates that ENSO and Rossby wave teleconnections can predict monsoon rainfall months ahead, showing the Pacific reach.

term:tlt.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:tlt.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:tlt.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:tlt.why: Explains El Nino variability through ocean temperature and stratification, with subsurface warming lagging surface warming.

term:tlt.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:tlt.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:tlt.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:tlt.why: Estimates Nino 3.4 anomalies with a filter that handles a warming climate, supporting the dashboard's own series.

term:trend.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:trend.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:trend.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:trend.why: Proposes anomaly and climate normal methods that account for warming trends, tested on sea surface temperatures.

term:u850.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:u850.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:u850.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:u850.why: Provides a real time method to estimate trade wind anomalies, applied to equatorial Pacific zonal and trade winds.

term:u850.title: Rotational and Irrotational Wind Forcing as dual drivers of El Nino Southern Oscillation variability
term:u850.our_title: Twin Winds: How Rotation and Divergence Drive El Niño
term:u850.oneliner: One part of the wind drives fast climate swings, the other drives slow decadal waves.
term:u850.why: Shows the wind stress component that drives thermocline shifts on interannual timescales, the engine linking weakened trades to ENSO.

term:weekly.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:weekly.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:weekly.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:weekly.why: Explains how Niño 3.4 SST anomalies can be estimated from climate normals, with caveats on standard 30-year baselines.

term:wwb.title: An improved noise model for representing westerly wind bursts in the recharge oscillator model of ENSO
term:wwb.our_title: The Noise That Rocks the Pacific Swing
term:wwb.oneliner: Bursts of westerly wind act like random pushes, and a new noise model explains why there are more of them before a big El Niño.
term:wwb.why: Models westerly wind bursts in an ENSO recharge oscillator and shows they amplify warm events, especially extreme El Niños.

term:wwv.title: Prediction Beyond the Medium Range with an Atmosphere-Ocean Model that Combines Physics-based Modeling and Machine Learning
term:wwv.our_title: A Translator That Learned the Language of the Ocean

term:wwv.why: Uses a model with top 300 meter ocean heat content to predict El Nino three to seven months ahead, showing this layer matters.

term:wwv.our_title: Predicting El Niño Six Months Ahead
term:wwv.oneliner: A hybrid neural network that combines spatial and temporal analysis of ocean data boosts El Niño forecast accuracy to 90%.
term:wwv.why: Adds subsurface ocean heat content to a deep learning model to improve El Nino prediction lead time.
